paragraphs.text: More fathers are taking paternity leave, but mothers are still doing all the work

sentences.text: More fathers are taking paternity leave, but mothers are still doing all the work

analysis.senseInContext: 父亲的、父职的（paternity leave 陪产假）
examples: He took paternity leave after the birth. 孩子出生后他休了陪产假。

more.confusables: paternity 父亲的 / maternity 母亲的；paternal 慈父般的

analysis.translationLiteral: 越来越多的父亲在休陪产假，但母亲仍然承担着所有的活儿。
analysis.translationNatural: 当爹的休陪产假越来越普遍，可家里的活还是当妈的全包。
analysis.structMarkup: 【More fathers】 _are taking_ ~paternity leave~, {but} 【mothers】 _are still doing_ ~all the work~.
analysis.structureSummary: 两个并列分句（but 转折）：主谓宾 + 主谓宾

components.part: are still doing all the work

clauses: but 连接两个并列分句，形成“表面进步、实质未变”的对照。
全句为标题式表达，省略了冠词等成分。

phrases.usage: paternity 父亲；对应 maternity leave（产假）。
phrases.example: He took two weeks of paternity leave. 他休了两周陪产假。

phrases.usage: 此处既指家务也指育儿，语气略带讽刺。
phrases.example: She does all the work and gets no credit. 活都是她干的，功劳却没有。

pitfalls: paternity（父亲的）与 maternity（母亲的）别混。
are taking / are doing 用进行时，强调趋势与现状。
analysis.paragraphRole: 以标题式判断开篇，点出全文张力：观念在变，但分工没变。

paragraphs.text: Attitudes towards paternity leave have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents.

sentences.text: Attitudes towards paternity leave have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents.

analysis.senseInContext: 父亲的、父职的（paternity leave 陪产假）
examples: He took paternity leave after the birth. 孩子出生后他休了陪产假。

more.confusables: paternity 父亲的 / maternity 母亲的；paternal 慈父般的

analysis.senseInContext: 偏见（gender bias persists 性别偏见依然存在）
examples: The study found bias in hiring. 研究发现招聘中存在偏见。

more.roots: 源自古法语 biais（斜的）→ 倾斜 → 偏向
more.confusables: bias 可指“偏差/偏好”；prejudice 贬义更重

analysis.translationLiteral: 根据一项针对职场父母的新研究，过去五年美国对陪产假的态度发生了剧烈变化，因为更多父亲愿意休较长假，但在职业前景和家庭方面，性别偏见依然存在。
analysis.translationNatural: 一项针对职场父母的新研究显示：过去五年美国人对陪产假的态度变化很大，越来越多父亲愿意休长假；但在职业前途与家庭分工上，性别偏见依旧。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Attitudes (towards paternity leave)】 _have drastically changed_ (in America) (in the last five years) {as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off}, {but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home}, (according to a new study of working parents).
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + as 原因状语从句 + but 并列分句 + according to 状语

components.note: 现在完成时，drastically 表程度

components.part: as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off
when it comes to career prospects and the home
components.note: when it comes to 是固定说法

components.part: according to a new study of working parents

clauses: as 引导原因状语从句（此处表“因为”，不是“当……时”）。
but 连接转折分句。
when it comes to... 是固定表达，后接名词。

phrases.meaning: 做某事感到自在/愿意做
phrases.usage: 后接动名词；comfortable 表心理上的接受。
phrases.example: She feels comfortable speaking in public. 她不怵当众讲话。

phrases.usage: extended time off 指“较长的假期”。
phrases.example: He took a month off work. 他休了一个月假。

phrases.usage: 后接名词或动名词。
phrases.example: When it comes to price, they win. 论价格，他们占优。

pitfalls: as 在此表原因，不是“当……时”。
feel comfortable taking：后接动名词。
persists（仍然存在）主语是 gender bias，用单数。
analysis.paragraphRole: 给出全文核心判断：态度变了，但偏见未消。

paragraphs.text: Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large US companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable.

sentences.text: Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large US companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable.

analysis.senseInContext: 可接受的、说得过去的（公司认为爸爸休陪产假没问题）
examples: Long hours are no longer acceptable. 长时间加班不再被接受。

analysis.translationLiteral: 波士顿学院工作与家庭中心的研究调查了四家美国大公司中有资格享受至少六周带薪育儿假的新父母，发现接受调查的 1240 名员工中有 81% 表示，父亲休假的观念已变得更容易被接受。
analysis.translationNatural: 波士顿学院“工作与家庭中心”调查了四家美国大公司里符合条件（至少六周带薪育儿假）的新手父母：1240 名受访员工中，81% 认为“父亲休假”这件事已经更容易被接受。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Research (by the Boston College Center for Work & Family), {which surveyed new parents at four large US companies {who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave}},】 _found_ ~{that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主语（带两层定语从句）+ 谓语 + 宾语从句（内含第二层宾语从句）

components.part: Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family
which surveyed new parents at four large US companies
who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave
that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said...
the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable

clauses: which surveyed... 是非限制性定语从句，修饰 research。
who were qualified for... 是定语从句，修饰 new parents。
that 81% of... said... 是宾语从句，作 found 的宾语。
the notion of... has become more acceptable 是省略 that 的宾语从句，作 said 的宾语。

phrases.usage: 后接名词或动名词；qualification 是名词。
phrases.example: She is qualified for the position. 她符合这个职位的资格。

phrases.usage: parental 父母的；paid 带薪的。
phrases.example: The company offers 12 weeks paid parental leave. 公司提供 12 周带薪育儿假。

phrases.usage: of 后接动名词。
phrases.example: The notion of working from home is now normal. 在家办公这一观念如今很常见。

pitfalls: 两层定语从句套在主语上，找主干时先抓 Research ... found that...。
employees surveyed 中 surveyed 是过去分词作后置定语。
the notion of fathers taking leave：of + 动名词复合结构。
analysis.paragraphRole: 给出调查数据：81% 认为父亲休假已被接受，支撑“态度变化”。

paragraphs.text: Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better.

sentences.text: Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better.

analysis.translationLiteral: 在受访者中，62% 的父亲休了最长假期，而母亲为 93%；约四分之三的员工表示雇主对父母双方休育儿假的支持是同等的，过半员工表示休假政策改善了职场文化。
analysis.translationNatural: 受访者里，62% 的父亲休满了最长假期，母亲则是 93%；约四分之三的人说公司对爸妈休育儿假的支持一样，超过一半的人说这些政策让职场文化变好了。
analysis.structMarkup: 【62% of fathers】 _took_ ~the maximum amount of time off~ (compared to 93% of mothers), {and} 【around three-quarters of workers】 _said_ ~{their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave}~ {and} 【over half】 _said_ ~{leave policies had made workplace culture better}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 三个并列分句：主谓宾 + 主谓宾从句 + 主谓宾从句

components.part: took the maximum amount of time off
their employer was equally supportive of...
leave policies had made workplace culture better
components.note: said 的宾语，用过去完成时

clauses: 三个分句由 and 连接，都是调查数据。
said 后省略 that，接宾语从句。
had made 用过去完成时，表示政策生效在“说”之前。

phrases.usage: 可作插入语或状语。
phrases.example: Compared to last year, sales doubled. 与去年相比销量翻倍。

phrases.usage: 形容词 supportive + of；动词 support。
phrases.example: Managers should be supportive of new ideas. 管理者应支持新想法。

phrases.usage: maximum 作形容词；反义 minimum。
phrases.example: Use the maximum amount of time allowed. 用足允许的最大时间。

pitfalls: 62% of fathers 作主语，谓语用复数 took。
equally supportive of mothers and fathers：equally 修饰 supportive。
had made 是过去完成时（政策效果先于受访者的评价）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用具体比例对照（62% vs 93%），揭示“父亲休假仍少于母亲”的现实。

paragraphs.text: The US is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue. So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws.

sentences.text: The US is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue.

analysis.senseInContext: 法定的（statutory paid leave 法定带薪假）
examples: Employees have statutory rights. 员工享有法定权利。

more.confusables: statutory 法定的；statuary 是“雕像”，拼写相近

analysis.translationLiteral: 美国是世界上仅有的三个不提供法定带薪假期的国家之一，但越来越多的州和公司开始着手解决这个问题。
analysis.translationNatural: 全球只有三个国家没有法定带薪假，美国是其中之一；不过越来越多的州和企业已经开始动手解决这事。
analysis.structMarkup: 【The US】 _is_ ~one of only three countries (in the world) (not to offer statutory paid leave)~, {but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue}.
analysis.structureSummary: 主系表（one of + 复数）+ but 并列分句

components.part: not to offer statutory paid leave
but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue
components.note: 转折：州与企业开始行动

clauses: one of + 复数名词作表语，谓语用单数 is。
but 连接转折分句。
take up 表示“着手处理”。

phrases.usage: statutory 法定的；statute 是法规。
phrases.example: Statutory holidays differ by country. 法定假日各国不同。

phrases.usage: take up 表“开始从事、接手”。
phrases.example: The committee took up the issue last week. 委员会上周着手处理该问题。

pitfalls: one of only three countries：谓语用单数 is。
not to offer... 是不定式作后置定语，修饰 countries。
take up 与 take on、take over 含义不同（此处为“着手处理”）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 指出制度背景：美国缺乏法定带薪假，但情况正在变化。

sentences.text: So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws.

analysis.translationLiteral: 到目前为止，八个州和哥伦比亚特区有自己的带薪家事假法律。
analysis.translationNatural: 到目前为止，已有八个州和哥伦比亚特区出台了带薪家事假法。
analysis.structMarkup: (So far), 【eight states and the District of Columbia】 _have_ ~their own paid family leave laws~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾结构（简单句）

components.note: 到目前为止（常配现在完成时）

components.part: eight states and the District of Columbia
components.note: 八个州 + 哥伦比亚特区（并列）

components.part: their own paid family leave laws

clauses: 本句是简单句，没有从句。

phrases.usage: 常与现在完成时连用。
phrases.example: So far, no one has complained. 到目前为止没人抱怨。

phrases.usage: 比 parental leave 范围更广。
phrases.example: Paid family leave helps new parents. 带薪家事假帮助新手父母。

pitfalls: so far 常配现在完成时（但此处 have 表状态）。
the District of Columbia 指华盛顿特区，不是“哥伦比亚国家”。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用具体数字说明制度层面的进展。

paragraphs.text: Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave. He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off.

sentences.text: Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave.

analysis.translationLiteral: 该中心的执行主任、这项研究的主要作者 Brad Harrington 估计，美国只有 20% 到 30% 的公司提供带薪育儿假。
analysis.translationNatural: 该中心执行主任、本研究第一作者 Brad Harrington 估计：全美只有 20% 到 30% 的公司提供带薪育儿假。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Brad Harrington, (executive director of the center) and (lead author of the study),】 _estimates_ ~{only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主语（带同位语）+ 谓语 + 宾语从句（省略 that）

components.part: executive director of the center and lead author of the study
only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave

clauses: estimates 后省略 that，引导宾语从句。
executive director of the center and lead author of the study 是同位语，解释 Brad Harrington 的身份。

phrases.usage: 机构职务名；director 董事/主任。
phrases.example: She is the executive director of the foundation. 她是该基金会的执行主任。

phrases.usage: 学术语境；对应 co-author（合著者）。
phrases.example: The lead author presented the findings. 第一作者介绍了研究结果。

pitfalls: estimates 后省略 that。
20% to 30% of companies 作从句主语，谓语用复数 offer。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用专家估算给出覆盖率现实：多数公司并没有这项福利。

sentences.text: He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off.

analysis.translationLiteral: 他认为这些研究结果反映了企业对新父亲休假态度的明显变化。
analysis.translationNatural: 他觉得这些发现说明：企业对“新爸爸休假”的态度确实有了明显转变。
analysis.structMarkup: 【He】 _feels_ ~{the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + 宾语从句（省略 that）

components.part: the research findings reflect an obvious change
in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off

clauses: feels 后省略 that，接宾语从句。
to new fathers taking time off 是介词短语，其中 taking time off 是动名词复合结构。

phrases.usage: reflect 表“反映、体现”。
phrases.example: The data reflects a shift in habits. 数据反映出习惯的转变。

phrases.usage: attitude to/towards + 名词。
phrases.example: Corporate attitudes to remote work vary. 企业对远程办公的态度各异。

pitfalls: feel 在此是“认为”，不是“感觉”。
attitudes to 后接动名词复合结构 new fathers taking time off。
analysis.paragraphRole: 引用专家判断，收束“态度确实在变”这一层意思。

paragraphs.text: "We did a study on paternity leave five years ago. Compared with those findings, these numbers were shocking to me. I did not expect 80% of people to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable and three-quarters to say it's equally supportive of women and men taking leave," Harrington said.

sentences.text: "We did a study on paternity leave five years ago.

analysis.senseInContext: 父亲的、父职的（paternity leave 陪产假）
examples: He took paternity leave after the birth. 孩子出生后他休了陪产假。

more.confusables: paternity 父亲的 / maternity 母亲的；paternal 慈父般的

analysis.translationLiteral: 我们在五年前做过一项关于陪产假的研究。
analysis.translationNatural: 五年前我们做过一个陪产假的研究。
analysis.structMarkup: 【We】 _did_ ~a study~ (on paternity leave) (five years ago).
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾 + 后置定语 + 时间状语

components.note: 第一人称复数，指研究团队
do a study 固定搭配中的动词部分
修饰 study，说明研究主题

clauses: 一般过去时 did：five years ago 是明确的过去时间点，不能用现在完成时。
on paternity leave 是介词短语作后置定语，修饰 study，不是修饰谓语 did。

phrases.usage: 也可说 conduct/carry out a study on sth，do 更口语。
phrases.example: They did a study on sleep patterns. 他们对睡眠模式做了一项研究。

phrases.meaning: 陪产假（父亲享有的育儿假）
phrases.usage: paternity 指父方；maternity leave 是产假；parental leave 是父母任一方都可休的育儿假。
phrases.example: He took two weeks of paternity leave. 他休了两周陪产假。

pitfalls: paternity（父方）易与 maternity（母方）、parental（父母通用）混用。
five years ago 与现在完成时冲突，此处必须一般过去时。
analysis.paragraphRole: 交代研究背景与时间坐标，为下文「与五年前对比」埋伏笔。

sentences.text: Compared with those findings, these numbers were shocking to me.

analysis.senseInContext: 令人震惊的、出乎意料的（形容数据）
examples: The figures were shocking to the researchers. 这些数字让研究者震惊。

analysis.translationLiteral: 与那些研究结果相比，这些数字对我来说是令人震惊的。
analysis.translationNatural: 跟那次的研究结果一比，这些数字让我很吃惊。
analysis.structMarkup: (Compared with those findings), 【these numbers】 _were_ ~shocking~ (to me).
analysis.structureSummary: 过去分词短语作状语 + 主系表

components.note: 过去分词短语，逻辑主语与主句主语 these numbers 一致
过去时，描述研究者当时的感受

clauses: 过去分词短语 Compared with... 作状语，逻辑主语须与主句主语一致（these numbers 被拿来比较）。
shocking 修饰物（令人震惊的），shocked 修饰人（感到震惊的）。

phrases.usage: 可置于句首作状语，也可插入句中；不要写成 Comparing with（主动形式会与主句主语错位）。
phrases.example: Compared with last year, profits rose 20%. 与去年相比，利润增长了 20%。

phrases.usage: 同类：be surprising/surprising to sb。
phrases.example: The result was shocking to everyone. 这个结果让所有人都震惊。

pitfalls: 误写 Comparing with those findings：主动分词要求逻辑主语是人，与 these numbers 不符。
shocking 与 shocked 用反：物用 -ing，人用 -ed。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用纵向对比把读者从「五年前」拉到现在，点出反差之大。

sentences.text: I did not expect 80% of people to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable and three-quarters to say it's equally supportive of women and men taking leave," Harrington said.

analysis.senseInContext: 可接受的、说得过去的（公司认为爸爸休陪产假没问题）
examples: Long hours are no longer acceptable. 长时间加班不再被接受。

analysis.translationLiteral: 哈林顿说：「我没有料到 80% 的人会说公司认为爸爸们休这个假是可以接受的，也没有料到四分之三的人会说公司对男女休假的支待是同等的。」
analysis.translationNatural: 哈林顿说：「我没料到有 80% 的人说公司觉得爸爸休这个假没问题，还有四分之三的人说公司对男女休假的支待是一样的。」
analysis.structMarkup: "【I】 _did not expect_ ~80% of people~ (to say {the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable}) {and} ~three-quarters~ (to say {it's equally supportive of women and men taking leave})," 【Harrington】 _said_.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾补（expect sb to do，两个并列）+ 转述主句

components.note: 否定 + 助动词 did 强调

components.part: to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable
components.note: expect sb to do 结构

components.part: the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable
to say it's equally supportive of women and men taking leave

clauses: expect sb to do sth：两个 to say 不定式并列，共享 expect。
find sth + adj.：find dads taking this leave acceptable 中 acceptable 是宾语补足语。
taking this leave / taking leave 是现在分词作后置定语，修饰 dads、women and men。
three-quarters 后承前省略 of people，避免重复。

phrases.usage: 否定形式 didn't expect sb to do 常用来表达「出乎意料」。
phrases.example: I didn't expect him to agree so quickly. 我没料到他会答应得这么快。

phrases.usage: 形容词作宾语补足语，不是副词。
phrases.example: I find the rule acceptable. 我觉得这条规定可以接受。

phrases.usage: supportive 是形容词，后接 of；动词形式是 support。
phrases.example: The company is supportive of working mothers. 公司支持职场妈妈。

paragraphs.text: The previous study found that nearly three-quarters of fathers saw two to four weeks as an appropriate duration for paternity leave and 76% said they would prefer not to take all their time off at once.

analysis.translationNatural: 之前那项研究发现，近四分之三的爸爸觉得陪产假两到四周比较合适，76% 的人说自己宁愿不把假一次用完。
analysis.structMarkup: 【The previous study】 _found_ ~that~ {nearly three-quarters of fathers saw two to four weeks as an appropriate duration for paternity leave} {and} 【76%】 _said_ {they would prefer not to take all their time off at once}.

pitfalls: at once 在本句不是「立刻」，而是「一次性」——这是全句最易错处。
an appropriate duration for...：appropriate 前用 an，因为 appropriate 以元音音素开头。
76% said：百分比作主语视为复数，谓语用 said 而非 was。
analysis.paragraphRole: 提供五年前的基准数据（时长偏好 + 不愿一次休完），与当下数据构成纵向对照。

paragraphs.text: Since then, there have been a number of legal cases against companies involving paternity leave—including cases against JPMorgan Chase and Estée Lauder—which have helped put pressure on companies to make their parental leave policies gender neutral.

sentences.text: Since then, there have been a number of legal cases against companies involving paternity leave—including cases against JPMorgan Chase and Estée Lauder—which have helped put pressure on companies to make their parental leave policies gender neutral.

analysis.senseInContext: 父亲的、父职的（paternity leave 陪产假）
examples: He took paternity leave after the birth. 孩子出生后他休了陪产假。

more.confusables: paternity 父亲的 / maternity 母亲的；paternal 慈父般的

analysis.senseInContext: 压力（舆论/法律对公司施加的推动力）

analysis.senseInContext: 中立的、不偏袒任何一方的（政策对男女同等）

analysis.translationLiteral: 自那以后，出现了若干起涉及陪产假的针对公司的法律案件——包括针对摩根大通和雅诗兰黛的案件——这些案件有助于向公司施压，使它们的育儿假政策实现性别中立。

analysis.structMarkup: (Since then), there _have been_ 【a number of legal cases】 (against companies) (involving paternity leave)—(including cases against JPMorgan Chase and Estée Lauder)—{which have helped put pressure on companies to make their parental leave policies gender neutral}.

help (to) do sth：本句 helped put 省略了 to。

phrases.text: put pressure on sb to do sth

phrases.meaning: 性别中立的（男女同等对待）
phrases.usage: 复合形容词，neutral 前不加连字符也常见；同义 gender-blind。
phrases.example: The policy is now gender neutral. 这项政策现在对男女一视同仁。

phrases.usage: 修饰可数名词复数，谓语用复数；the number of 则是「……的数量」，谓语用单数。

which 的先行词是 cases 而非 companies——它施压的是公司，但先行词是案件。

analysis.paragraphRole: 交代外部推动力——法律诉讼，为下文「制度变了但观念没跟上」做铺垫。

paragraphs.text: However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home—even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality.

sentences.text: However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home—even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality.

analysis.translationLiteral: 然而，这项研究还显示出传统性别角色在工作和家庭两方面如何延续——在工作场所，报告职业潜力认知发生变化的女性多于男性；在家庭中也是如此，甚至在那些声称强烈渴望平等的员工中也不例外。
analysis.translationNatural: 但研究也表明，传统的性别分工在工作上和家里都还在延续：职场上，说自己对职业前景的看法变了的女性比男性多；家里也一样，连那些嘴上说特别想要平等的人都逃不掉。
analysis.structMarkup: (However), 【the study】 _also shows_ ~how traditional gender roles endure~ (both at work), {where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential}, {and at home}—(even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality).

components.note: 与此前的乐观数据形成转折
一般现在时，陈述研究结论
how 引导，作 shows 的宾语

clauses: how 引导宾语从句，作 shows 的宾语，意为「……如何/以何种方式」。
both … and … 连接两个并列状语 at work 与 at home，and 前有破折号插入。

more women than men 是比较结构作主语，谓语用复数 reported。
who claim to have... 定语从句修饰 workers。

phrases.meaning: 在工作场所 / 在家里
phrases.usage: 两个介词短语常成对出现，表「职场与家庭」两个领域。

phrases.usage: desire 后可接 for + 名词，或 to do / that 从句。

phrases.usage: claim 后接不定式，不用 claim doing。

paragraphs.text: The vast majority of men, 97%, said one of the top reasons to take leave was to share caregiving with their partner. But when they were asked about how caregiving and household tasks were divided, their answers painted a different picture. While about 75% of employees said both genders should give the same amount of care, the majority of men and nearly half of women admitted that in reality the female actually did most of it. A tiny fraction, 2%, of men said they did more of the childcare.

sentences.text: The vast majority of men, 97%, said one of the top reasons to take leave was to share caregiving with their partner.

paragraphs.text: Men and women's experiences of the return to work following parental leave were also considerably different. Of the women surveyed, 32% reported a downturn in their job satisfaction, while 14% said it increased. In comparison, 17% of men said their job satisfaction went down and 20% said it went up. Meanwhile, more women reported an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations after childbirth. Half of the women said they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent, while just 27% of men did. Similar percentages of men and women said they enjoyed their careers and that it gave them a sense of achievement, while around half of women and 44% of men said it was a key part of their identity.

analysis.senseInContext: 下滑、下降（工作满意度下降）
examples: The industry faces a serious downturn. 这个行业面临严重下滑。

analysis.translationLiteral: 在受访女性中，32% 报告工作满意度下降，而 14% 说上升了。
analysis.translationNatural: 受访女性里，32% 说自己的工作满意度下降了，14% 说反而上升了。
analysis.structMarkup: (Of the women surveyed), 【32%】 _reported_ ~a downturn in their job satisfaction~, {while} 【14%】 _said_ {it increased}.
analysis.structureSummary: 状语 + 主谓宾 + while 并列对照分句

components.note: surveyed 是过去分词后置定语，修饰 women

components.part: a downturn in their job satisfaction

clauses: Of the women surveyed 置于句首作范围限定，相当于「在……之中」。
while 连接两个对照分句，表「而、然而」。
it increased 中的 it 指前文的 job satisfaction，避免重复。

phrases.usage: 常搭 economic downturn（经济衰退）；反义 an upturn。
phrases.example: There was a sharp downturn in sales. 销量急剧下滑。

phrases.usage: 不可数名词短语，常与 report/show/improve 搭配。
phrases.example: Flexible hours raise job satisfaction. 弹性工时会提高工作满意度。

pitfalls: 32% reported：百分比作主语视为复数，谓语不加 -s。
downturn 后接 in，不接 of 更常见。
while 在此不是「当……时」，而是对比连词。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用第一组男女对照数据（女性满意度下滑更多）支撑段首论断。

sentences.text: In comparison, 17% of men said their job satisfaction went down and 20% said it went up.

analysis.translationLiteral: 相比之下，17% 的男性说工作满意度下降了，20% 说上升了。
analysis.translationNatural: 相比之下，17% 的男性说自己满意度下降，20% 说上升了。
analysis.structMarkup: (In comparison), 【17% of men】 _said_ ~{their job satisfaction went down}~ {and} 【20%】 _said_ {it went up}.
analysis.structureSummary: 状语 + 两个并列主谓宾结构

components.note: 与前一句的女性数据对照

clauses: 两个分句由 and 连接，第二个分句的 said 后同样省略 that。
go down / go up 是系表性动词短语，表变化方向，比 decrease/increase 更口语。
20% 后承前省略 of men，避免重复。

phrases.usage: 独立使用作状语；后接 with/to 时表「与……相比」。
phrases.example: In comparison, men reported fewer problems. 相比之下，男性报告的问题更少。

phrases.usage: 口语化表达，可指数值、价格、情绪；正式文体多用 decrease/increase。
phrases.example: Prices went up again. 价格又涨了。

pitfalls: in comparison 单独使用，不接宾语；in comparison with 才接。
went down 与 went up 都是不及物用法。
20% 后省略 of men，不要误以为指全部员工。
analysis.paragraphRole: 紧跟上句给出男性对照数据，凸显「女性下滑更明显」。

sentences.text: Meanwhile, more women reported an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations after childbirth.

analysis.translationLiteral: 同时，更多女性报告在生育后职责与管理者期望有所增加。
analysis.translationNatural: 与此同时，更多女性说自己生完孩子后，责任和领导对她的期待都变高了。
analysis.structMarkup: (Meanwhile), 【more women】 _reported_ ~an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations~ (after childbirth).
analysis.structureSummary: 状语 + 主谓宾 + 时间状语

components.note: 更多女性（与前文男性数据相对）

components.part: an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations
components.note: in 后接两个并列名词

clauses: more women 是比较级主语，谓语用复数 reported。
an increase in A and B：介词 in 同时支配两个并列宾语。
manager expectations 指「管理者（对她）的期望」，所有格省略。

phrases.usage: increase 作名词时接 in；作动词时 increase 可直接及物。
phrases.example: There was an increase in demand. 需求有所增加。

phrases.usage: childbirth 不可数；同义 after giving birth。
phrases.example: Many women return to work soon after childbirth. 许多女性生育后不久就返岗。

pitfalls: increase in（名词）与 increase（动词）后接方式不同，别写成 an increase of responsibilities（of 常用于具体数值）。
responsibilities 用复数，指具体职责。
manager expectations 中间没有 's，是「管理者期望」的复合名词用法。
analysis.paragraphRole: 补充女性返岗后的额外压力来源（责任与期待上升），解释满意度下滑的原因。

sentences.text: Half of the women said they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent, while just 27% of men did.

analysis.senseInContext: 灵活的、弹性的（弹性工作安排）
examples: We offer flexible hours to parents. 我们为父母提供弹性工时。

analysis.translationLiteral: 半数女性说她们在成为父母后使用过弹性工作安排，而男性仅 27%。
analysis.translationNatural: 一半的女性说自己当妈以后用过弹性工作安排，男性只有 27% 这么做。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Half of the women】 _said_ ~{they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent}~, {while} 【just 27% of men】 _did_.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾从句 + while 对照分句（用代动词 did）

components.part: they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent

components.note: did 替代 used flexible work arrangements

clauses: Half of the women 作主语时谓语用单数或复数均可，此处原文用复数 said。
after 是介词，后接动名词 becoming；不接从句。
did 是代动词，替代前面的 used flexible work arrangements，避免重复。
just 修饰 27%，强调比例之低。

phrases.usage: 包括弹性工时、远程办公等；也可说 flexible working。
phrases.example: Flexible work arrangements help parents. 弹性工作安排对父母有帮助。

phrases.usage: 中性表达，涵盖父母双方；比 become a mother/father 更概括。
phrases.example: Your priorities change when you become a parent. 有了孩子后你的优先级会变。

pitfalls: after becoming 是介词 + 动名词；误写 after become 就错了。
did 是代动词，不能换成 made 或 took。
just 27% 的 just 表「仅仅」，不是「刚刚」。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用弹性工作的使用率差异，量化「育儿负担仍主要落在女性身上」。

sentences.text: Similar percentages of men and women said they enjoyed their careers and that it gave them a sense of achievement, while around half of women and 44% of men said it was a key part of their identity.

analysis.senseInContext: 成就、成绩（职业带来的成就感）
examples: Winning the award was a huge achievement. 获奖是巨大的成就。

analysis.senseInContext: 自我认同、身份感（职业是「我是谁」的重要部分）
examples: Work is central to his identity. 工作是他自我认同的核心。

analysis.translationLiteral: 相近比例的男性和女性说他们喜欢自己的职业，且职业给了他们成就感；而约半数女性和 44% 的男性说职业是自我认同的关键部分。
analysis.translationNatural: 男女中都有相近比例的人说自己喜欢这份职业、职业带来成就感；约一半女性和 44% 的男性说，职业是「自己是谁」的重要部分。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Similar percentages of men and women】 _said_ ~{they enjoyed their careers}~ {and} ~that {it gave them a sense of achievement}~, {while} 【around half of women and 44% of men】 _said_ {it was a key part of their identity}.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + 两个并列宾语从句 + while 对照分句（内含宾语从句）

components.part: Similar percentages of men and women

components.note: 支配两个 that 从句

components.part: that it gave them a sense of achievement
components.note: 保留 that，与从句1 并列

components.part: around half of women and 44% of men
it was a key part of their identity

clauses: 两个宾语从句并列：第一个省略 that，第二个保留 that，这是正式文体的常见写法。
while 引导对照分句，表「而」。
it 两次出现都指 career（职业），不是公司或工作单位。
a sense of achievement：of + 抽象名词，表「……感」。

phrases.usage: sense of + 抽象名词：a sense of responsibility/pride/belonging。
phrases.example: Finishing the project gave her a sense of achievement. 完成项目让她很有成就感。

phrases.usage: key 作形容词表「关键的」；同义 an essential part of。
phrases.example: Trust is a key part of teamwork. 信任是团队合作的关键。

phrases.usage: percentage 与具体数字连用时谓语单复数看 of 后的名词。
phrases.example: Similar percentages of both groups agreed. 两组中同比例的人表示同意。

pitfalls: 第二个宾语从句保留 that，是为避免与第一个从句混淆——写作时不要随意省略。
identity 在此指「自我认同、身份感」，不是「身份证」。
around half of women and 44% of men 是并列主语，谓语用 said（复数）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 指出男女在「职业认同」上差别不大，反衬真正差异在「机会与家庭分工」，避免读者误读为全面对立。

paragraphs.text: On the subject of career advancement, 59% of women and 49% of men said leave could be limiting and both genders said they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term. But on opportunity for promotion, more than double the number of women, 30% compared with 15% of men, believed their chances to be lower after becoming a parent. Despite progress, the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power is demonstrated in this year's Fortune 500 list, which featured a record 33 female CEOs, but this still represents a tiny fraction of the total.

sentences.text: On the subject of career advancement, 59% of women and 49% of men said leave could be limiting and both genders said they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term.

analysis.senseInContext: 晋升、发展（职业向上推进）
examples: Training supports career advancement. 培训有助于职业发展。

analysis.senseInContext: 影响、冲击（对长期发展的影响）
examples: The policy had little impact on hiring. 该政策对招聘影响很小。

more.roots: im-（向内）+ pact（压紧）→ 撞击 → 影响
confusables: impact 作动词时可直接接宾语

analysis.translationLiteral: 就职业晋升而言，59% 的女性和 49% 的男性说休假可能有限制作用，且两性都说他们担心这会对自己的长期发展产生影响。
analysis.translationNatural: 说到升职，59% 的女性和 49% 的男性都说休假可能会拖后腿，而且男女都担心这会影响到自己的长远发展。
analysis.structMarkup: (On the subject of career advancement), 【59% of women and 49% of men】 _said_ ~{leave could be limiting}~ {and} 【both genders】 _said_ {they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term}.
analysis.structureSummary: 话题状语 + 两个并列主谓宾从句结构

components.part: On the subject of career advancement
they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term
components.note: 内含 feared 的宾语从句（省略 that）

clauses: on the subject of 是话题转换的固定表达，后接名词或动名词。
could be limiting：could 表「有可能」，limiting 作表语形容词。
feared (that) it would have...：feared 后又套一层宾语从句，would 表过去将来。
long-term 是副词性用法，修饰整个谓语部分，置于句末。

phrases.usage: 用于转换话题，比 about 更正式。
phrases.example: On the subject of pay, nothing has been decided. 关于薪酬，还没有定论。

phrases.usage: impact 可数，用 an；同义 affect（及物，不加 on）。
phrases.example: Long hours have an impact on health. 长时间工作影响健康。

phrases.usage: advancement 不可数，比 promotion（一次升职）更宽泛。
phrases.example: She moved abroad for career advancement. 她为职业发展移居国外。

pitfalls: have an impact on：impact 是可数名词，别漏掉 an；也别写成 impact on 前用动词 affect 还加 on。
both genders 后的 they 指两性整体，谓语用复数。
long-term 在此作副词，不是形容词；作定语时用 long-term prospects。
analysis.paragraphRole: 引入「休假对晋升的影响」这一顾虑，为下一句的性别差异埋点。

sentences.text: But on opportunity for promotion, more than double the number of women, 30% compared with 15% of men, believed their chances to be lower after becoming a parent.

analysis.senseInContext: 晋升（职位提升的机会）
examples: She earned a promotion last year. 她去年获得晋升。

more.roots: pro-（向前）+ movere（移动）→ 向前推

analysis.translationLiteral: 但在晋升机会上，认为成为父母后自己机会更低的女性的数量是男性的两倍多——30% 对 15%。
analysis.translationNatural: 但说到升职机会，觉得当爸妈后自己机会变小的女性是男性的两倍多——女性 30%，男性 15%。
analysis.structMarkup: (But) (on opportunity for promotion), 【more than double the number of women】, (30% compared with 15% of men), _believed_ ~their chances to be lower after becoming a parent~.
analysis.structureSummary: 状语 + 主语（带插入比例）+ 谓语 + 宾语补足结构

components.note: 与上句的「两性都担心」形成对比

components.part: more than double the number of women
components.note: 女性人数是（男性）两倍多
believe sth to be + adj. 结构

clauses: more than double the number of women：double 在此作前置限定，意为「两倍于」。
believe sth to be + adj.：不定式作宾语补足语，比 believe that 从句更简洁。
30% compared with 15% of men 是插入语，过去分词 compared with 表对比。
after becoming a parent：介词 after + 动名词。

phrases.usage: double 作限定词直接修饰名词；动词用法 double（翻倍）不加 the。
phrases.example: The firm hired double the number of graduates. 公司招了双倍数量的毕业生。

phrases.usage: 插入语形式，常用于给出对照数据。
phrases.example: Sales rose 12%, compared with 5% last year. 销量增长 12%，去年为 5%。

phrases.usage: 正式结构，被动形式为 sth is believed to be。
phrases.example: Experts believe the risk to be low. 专家认为风险很低。

pitfalls: double the number：double 前不加 a，也不说 double of the number。
believed their chances to be lower：不能说 believed their chances were lower 之外的错误形式 believed to be lower their chances。
30% compared with 15% of men：比较对象要平行（女性比例 vs 男性比例）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 把「担心」量化为「女性感受到的晋升损失是男性两倍」，是职场落差的核心数据。

sentences.text: Despite progress, the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power is demonstrated in this year's Fortune 500 list, which featured a record 33 female CEOs, but this still represents a tiny fraction of the total.

analysis.senseInContext: 一小部分（2% 的男性，极小比例）
examples: Only a fraction of the budget was used. 只用了预算的一小部分。

more.roots: fract（打碎）+ -ion → 碎片 → 分数

analysis.translationLiteral: 尽管有进步，女性争取最高权力职位的艰难仍体现在今年的《财富》500 强榜单上——该榜单有创纪录的 33 位女性 CEO，但这仍只占总数极小一部分。
analysis.translationNatural: 进步是有的，但女性要爬到最高层有多难，今年的《财富》500 强榜单就是证明：女性 CEO 有 33 位，创了纪录，可放在总数里仍然只是极小一部分。
analysis.structMarkup: (Despite progress), 【the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power】 _is demonstrated_ ~(in this year's Fortune 500 list)~, {which featured a record 33 female CEOs}, {but} 【this】 _still represents_ ~a tiny fraction of the total~.
analysis.structureSummary: 让步状语 + 主谓被动 + which 非限制性定语从句 + but 并列转折分句

components.part: the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power
components.note: for women to reach 是不定式复合结构作后置定语

components.part: which featured a record 33 female CEOs
but this still represents a tiny fraction of the total
components.note: this 指 33 位女性 CEO 这一事实

clauses: Despite + 名词（progress）：若用从句须改成 Although there has been progress。
the struggle for women to reach...：for + 名词 + 不定式，说明不定式的逻辑主语。
which 引导非限制性定语从句，先行词是 list。
this 指代前面整个事实（33 位女性 CEO），不是 list。

phrases.usage: 介词，后接名词/动名词；后接从句要用 although/though。
phrases.example: Despite the rain, they went out. 尽管下雨，他们还是出门了。

phrases.usage: of + 抽象名词作后置定语；也可说 powerful positions。
phrases.example: Few women hold positions of power. 女性担任要职的很少。

phrases.text: a tiny fraction of the total
phrases.usage: 常用作收束性判断，强调比例之低。
phrases.example: Women make up a tiny fraction of the total. 女性只占总数的极小部分。

pitfalls: Despite 后不能接句子；接句子要用 Although/Even though。
a record 33 female CEOs：record 作前置形容词表「创纪录的」，不加 a record of。
this 指代的是「33 位女性 CEO」这一事实，而不是 list。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用榜单数据把「进步」与「仍然极少」并置，避免读者把前面的改革成效读成已解决问题。

paragraphs.text: Harrington said culture change depends on companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities. "By that I mean companies need to give men paternity leave and encourage men to take time off to be with their kids early on in the kids' life. They also need to recognise that men have to make significant adjustments when they become parents. Companies cannot do all these things to enhance women's advancement and then turn around and say, 'Oh, but we don't expect the men to take over for the women at home.'"

sentences.text: Harrington said culture change depends on companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities.

analysis.translationLiteral: 哈林顿说，文化变革取决于公司是否更关注男性及其责任。
analysis.translationNatural: 哈林顿说，要改变这种文化，关键是公司得更多地把目光放在男性身上、放在他们要担的责任上。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Harrington】 _said_ ~{culture change depends on companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + 宾语从句（从句为 depend on + 动名词复合结构）

components.part: companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities
components.note: companies 是 putting 的逻辑主语

clauses: depend on + 动名词复合结构：companies putting... 中 companies 是 putting 的逻辑主语，不能改成 companies put。
put focus on sth：把重点放在……上；同义 focus on sth。
their responsibilities 中的 their 指 men，不是 companies。

phrases.usage: 后接名词或动名词；后接从句时用 depend on it that...。
phrases.example: Success depends on preparation. 成功取决于准备。

phrases.usage: focus 不可数；也可说 place/lay emphasis on。
phrases.example: The firm puts more focus on retention. 公司更关注员工留存。

pitfalls: depend on companies putting：动名词复合结构，不能写成 depend on companies put。
their 的指代对象是 men——代词指代是本题型高频陷阱。
focus 不可数，不说 a focus on（作可数时指「焦点」这一具体点，另当别论）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 引出解决方案的第一条：文化变革的着力点在男性，而非只关注女性。

sentences.text: "By that I mean companies need to give men paternity leave and encourage men to take time off to be with their kids early on in the kids' life.

analysis.senseInContext: 父亲的、父职的（paternity leave 陪产假）
examples: He took paternity leave after the birth. 孩子出生后他休了陪产假。

more.confusables: paternity 父亲的 / maternity 母亲的；paternal 慈父般的

analysis.translationLiteral: 我的意思是，公司需要给男性陪产假，并鼓励男性在孩子年幼时休假去陪伴他们。
analysis.translationNatural: 我指的是，公司得给爸爸们陪产假，还得鼓励他们在孩子小的时候就休假陪孩子。
analysis.structMarkup: " (By that) 【I】 _mean_ ~{companies need to give men paternity leave and encourage men to take time off to be with their kids early on in the kids' life}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 状语 + 主谓 + 宾语从句（从句内含并列谓语）

components.part: companies need to give... and encourage...
early on in the kids' life

clauses: By that I mean...：倒装式固定表达，用于澄清上一句的意思。
need to give ... and encourage ...：两个不定式并列，共享 need to。
take time off to be with sb：不定式表目的。
early on in the kids' life：early on 是固定短语「在早期」，in the kids' life 进一步限定。

phrases.usage: 口语常用，后接完整从句；也可说 what I mean is...。
phrases.example: By that I mean we need more time. 我的意思是我们需要更多时间。

phrases.usage: time off 是名词短语；take time off to do sth 表请假去做某事。
phrases.example: He took time off to care for his son. 他请假照顾儿子。

phrases.usage: 副词短语，常后接 in + 时间段。
phrases.example: We spotted the problem early on. 我们很早就发现了问题。

pitfalls: take time off 不加 a，也不说 take off time。
early on 的 on 不能省略，early 单独作副词意思不同。
kids' life：复数所有格 kids'，不是 kid's。
analysis.paragraphRole: 把「关注男性」具体化为两条措施：给假、鼓励早休假。

sentences.text: They also need to recognise that men have to make significant adjustments when they become parents.

analysis.translationLiteral: 他们还需要认识到，男性在成为父母时必须做出重大调整。
analysis.translationNatural: 公司还得明白，男性当了爸爸也得做出很大的调整。
analysis.structMarkup: 【They】 _also need to recognise_ ~{that}~ {men have to make significant adjustments when they become parents}.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + that 宾语从句（从句内含时间状语从句）

components.part: that men have to make significant adjustments

clauses: need to recognise：recognise 后常接 that 从句，也可接名词。
make adjustments：adjustment 可数，make 是固定搭配（不说 do adjustments）。
when they become parents：they 指 men，不是 companies。

phrases.usage: adjustment 可数，常与 make 搭配；同义 adjust（动词）。
phrases.example: Staff had to make adjustments to the new system. 员工不得不适应新系统。

phrases.usage: 后接从句；美式拼写 recognize。
phrases.example: We recognise that change takes time. 我们认识到改变需要时间。

pitfalls: make adjustments 不用 do；单数用 make an adjustment。
recognise 与 realize 近义，但 recognise 侧重「承认/认可」。
they 在此指 men；代词指代必须回看上一句确定。
analysis.paragraphRole: 补充「观念层面」的要求：公司要承认男性同样面临身份转变。

sentences.text: Companies cannot do all these things to enhance women's advancement and then turn around and say, 'Oh, but we don't expect the men to take over for the women at home.'"

analysis.senseInContext: 促进、提升（促进女性职业发展）
examples: Good lighting enhances the space. 好的照明能提升空间感。

confusables: enhance 不接 sb to do

analysis.senseInContext: 晋升、发展（职业向上推进）
examples: Training supports career advancement. 培训有助于职业发展。

analysis.translationLiteral: 公司不能一边做所有这些事来促进女性发展，一边又转身说：「哦，但我们并不指望男性在家接替女性。」
analysis.translationNatural: 公司不能一边喊着帮女性往上走，一边回头说「哦，可我们没打算让男的在家里接女性的班」。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Companies】 _cannot_ _do_ ~all these things~ (to enhance women's advancement) {and} _then turn around and say_, ~'Oh, but we don't expect the men to take over for the women at home.'~
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾 + 目的不定式 + and 连接第二个谓语 + 引语宾语

components.part: and then turn around and say
'Oh, but we don't expect the men to take over...'

clauses: cannot do ... and then turn around and say：cannot 否定的是整个并列动作，意为「不能既……又……」。
turn around 在此是比喻用法，表「掉头改口、反过来」。
expect sb to do sth：expect 后接宾语 + 不定式。
take over for sb：替某人接手。

phrases.meaning: 反过来又说、转身改口说
phrases.usage: 口语比喻，常含批评意味，指前后矛盾。
phrases.example: You can't promise help and then turn around and say no. 你不能先答应帮忙又反口说不。

phrases.usage: take over 可单独用（接管），for sb 说明替代对象。
phrases.example: She took over for him while he was away. 他不在时由她接手。

phrases.usage: 及物动词，后接名词；同义 improve/boost。
phrases.example: Training enhances skills. 培训能提升技能。

pitfalls: cannot ... and then ...：否定覆盖并列整体，字面「不能做A又做B」= 「不能自相矛盾」。
the men / the women：加 the 表群体，泛指一类人。
turn around 不能按字面理解为「转身」这一动作。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用直接引语收束论点，把「制度性支持」与「家庭分工期待」的自相矛盾点破。

paragraphs.text: In May, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP announced a historic class-action $5m settlement with JPMorgan Chase on behalf of male employees who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave. Derek Rotondo, 35, filed the discrimination charge against his company after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers. Thus, they were allowed to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Fathers, however, could take just two weeks.

sentences.text: In May, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP announced a historic class-action $5m settlement with JPMorgan Chase on behalf of male employees who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave.

analysis.senseInContext: （法律）和解；和解金
examples: The two sides reached a settlement. 双方达成了和解。

analysis.translationLiteral: 今年 5 月，美国公民自由联盟（ACLU）与 Outten & Golden 律师事务所代表男性员工宣布与摩根大通达成为一起历史性的集体诉讼和解，金额 500 万美元——这些员工称自己被非法剥夺了带薪育儿假。
analysis.translationNatural: 今年 5 月，美国公民自由联盟和 Outten & Golden 律所代表一群男员工，跟摩根大通达成了 500 万美元的集体诉讼和解——这些人说自己被非法剥夺了带薪育儿假。
analysis.structMarkup: (In May), 【the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP】 _announced_ ~a historic class-action $5m settlement~ (with JPMorgan Chase) (on behalf of male employees) {who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave}.
analysis.structureSummary: 时间状语 + 并列主语 + 主谓宾 + 两个修饰语 + who 定语从句

components.note: 今年 5 月（依上文时态判断）

components.part: the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP

components.note: class-action 作前置定语，settlement 是中心词
修饰 settlement，说明与谁达成

components.part: who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave

clauses: on behalf of sb：代表某人（的利益），后接名词。
who 引导定语从句修饰 male employees，从句内又套 claim 的宾语从句。
be denied access to sth：被剥夺获得……的权利，被动结构。
class-action 是复合形容词，修饰 settlement（集体诉讼和解）。

phrases.usage: 后接名词或代词；常用于法律与正式场合。
phrases.example: She accepted the award on behalf of the team. 她代表团队领奖。

phrases.usage: deny sb sth 的被动形式；access 后接 to。
phrases.example: Students were denied access to the lab. 学生被拒绝进入实验室。

phrases.usage: 法律术语；class action 指一群人共同提起的诉讼。
phrases.example: The company agreed to a class-action settlement. 公司同意集体诉讼和解。

pitfalls: a historic class-action $5m settlement：多个前置修饰叠加，中心词是 settlement。
$5m 读作 five million dollars，作定语时不用复数 dollars。
be denied access to：不是 be denied to access。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用例证（真实诉讼与和解金额）说明前文所述「法律施压」确有实效。

sentences.text: Derek Rotondo, 35, filed the discrimination charge against his company after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers.

analysis.senseInContext: 歧视（因性别而在育儿假上区别对待）
examples: The law bans discrimination at work. 法律禁止职场歧视。

more.roots: dis-（分开）+ crimen（区分）→ 区别对待

analysis.translationLiteral: 35 岁的德里克·罗通多在其公司被指控后提起了歧视指控——据称他的人事部门告诉他，母亲被视为主要照护者。
analysis.translationNatural: 35 岁的德里克·罗通多对公司提出了歧视指控——因为据称 HR 告诉他，公司把妈妈当作主要照护人。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Derek Rotondo】, (35), _filed_ ~the discrimination charge~ (against his company) {after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers}.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾 + 时间状语从句（内含被动 + 宾语从句）

components.note: file a charge 提起诉讼/指控

components.part: after he was allegedly told by his HR department that...

clauses: file a charge against sb：对某人提出指控，法律固定搭配。
after 引导时间状语从句，从句为被动语态 he was told by...。
be told that...：tell sb that 的被动形式。
mothers were considered primary caregivers：consider sb (to be) sth 的被动。

phrases.usage: 法律语境固定搭配；charge 可换 complaint/lawsuit。
phrases.example: She filed a complaint against her manager. 她对经理提出了投诉。

phrases.usage: allegedly 表「据称、未经证实」，新闻法律文体常用。
phrases.example: He was allegedly paid in cash. 据称他是收现金的。

phrases.usage: consider sb/sth (to be) + 名词/形容词的被动式。
phrases.example: Remote staff are considered full members. 远程员工被视为正式成员。

pitfalls: allegedly 修饰「被告诉」这一事实未经证实，不能理解为「肯定」。
primary caregivers 用复数，与 mothers 一致。
filed 后接 the discrimination charge，charge 在此可数。
analysis.paragraphRole: 给出具体当事人与事由，把抽象诉讼落到一个人的遭遇上。

sentences.text: Thus, they were allowed to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave.

analysis.translationLiteral: 因此，她们被允许休 16 周带薪育儿假。
analysis.translationNatural: 所以，她们（母亲们）可以休 16 周带薪育儿假。
analysis.structMarkup: (Thus), 【they】 _were allowed_ ~to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave~.
analysis.structureSummary: 结果状语 + 主谓（被动）+ 不定式补足

components.note: allow sb to do 的被动

components.part: to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave
components.note: 被动句中原来作宾补的不定式变为主补

clauses: allow sb to do sth 变被动后为 sb is allowed to do sth。
16 weeks of paid parental leave：数量表达，weeks 用复数。
Thus 表结果，承接上句「母亲被视为主要照护者」这一前提。

phrases.usage: allow sb to do 的被动式；不要写成 be allowed doing。
phrases.example: Staff are allowed to work from home. 员工被允许居家办公。

phrases.usage: paid 修饰 leave；unpaid leave 为无薪假。
phrases.example: The firm offers 12 weeks of paid parental leave. 公司提供 12 周带薪育儿假。

pitfalls: they 指母亲（mothers），不是男员工——与下句 fathers 对照才能读通。
be allowed to do，不能写 be allowed doing。
16 weeks of：数量短语，weeks 必须复数。
analysis.paragraphRole: 交代制度差异的具体数字（母亲 16 周），为下句「父亲只有 2 周」制造落差。

sentences.text: Fathers, however, could take just two weeks.

analysis.translationLiteral: 然而，父亲们只能休两周。
analysis.translationNatural: 可父亲这边，只能休两周。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Fathers】, (however), _could take_ ~just two weeks~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓宾（带插入转折副词）

components.note: 父亲们，与上句 they（母亲）对照
could 表过去被允许/可以

clauses: however 作插入语时前后加逗号；作连词时须置于句首且有分号或句号分隔。
could 在此表过去的许可（= were allowed to），不是虚拟语气。
just 修饰 two weeks，强调差距之大。

phrases.usage: just 在此等于 only，表「仅仅」。
phrases.example: They gave him just two days to decide. 他们只给了他两天决定。

phrases.usage: 作前置定语时用连字符且 week 用单数；单独作宾语时则说 two weeks of leave。
phrases.example: He was granted a two-week leave. 他获批两周假期。

pitfalls: however 作插入语不能像 but 那样直接连接两个分句。
could 此处是过去许可，不是「可能」。
two weeks 前不加 a（应为 a two-week leave 才对）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用极简短句收束对比：16 周 vs 2 周，制度性不平等的证据落地。

paragraphs.text: The father of two from Columbus, Ohio, who still works at the company as an associate and investigator, said he has witnessed a "domino effect" across companies since the settlement, but that there is still substantial progress to be made towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave.

sentences.text: The father of two from Columbus, Ohio, who still works at the company as an associate and investigator, said he has witnessed a "domino effect" across companies since the settlement, but that there is still substantial progress to be made towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave.

analysis.senseInContext: （法律）和解；和解金
examples: The two sides reached a settlement. 双方达成了和解。

analysis.senseInContext: 大量的、实质性的（仍有大量进展要做）
examples: There has been substantial improvement. 已有实质性改善。

analysis.senseInContext: 父亲的、父职的（paternity leave 陪产假）
examples: He took paternity leave after the birth. 孩子出生后他休了陪产假。

more.confusables: paternity 父亲的 / maternity 母亲的；paternal 慈父般的

analysis.translationLiteral: 这位来自俄亥俄州哥伦布市、育有两个孩子、至今仍在该公司担任副理与调查员的父亲说，自和解以来他目睹了各公司之间的「多米诺效应」，但在改变人们对陪产假的态度上仍有大量进展要做。
analysis.translationNatural: 这位住在俄亥俄州哥伦布、有两个孩子、现在还在这家公司做副理兼调查员的父亲说，和解之后他看到各家公司像推倒多米诺骨牌一样接连改变；不过他也说，要真正改变人们对陪产假的看法，还有很长的路要走。
analysis.structMarkup: 【The father of two from Columbus, Ohio】, {who still works at the company as an associate and investigator}, _said_ ~{he has witnessed a "domino effect" across companies since the settlement}~, {but} ~that {there is still substantial progress to be made towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主语（带定语从句）+ 谓语 + 两个并列宾语从句（第二个由 but 转折并保留 that）

components.part: The father of two from Columbus, Ohio
components.note: 中心词 father of two，后接籍贯

components.part: who still works at the company as an associate and investigator
he has witnessed a "domino effect" across companies since the settlement
components.note: 现在完成时，since 为标志

components.part: but that there is still substantial progress to be made...
components.note: but 转折 + 保留 that

components.part: towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave

clauses: 两个宾语从句由 but 连接：第一个省略 that，第二个保留 that，避免歧义。
has witnessed：since the settlement 是现在完成时标志。
progress to be made：不定式被动作后置定语，表「尚待取得的」。
attitudes towards sth：对……的态度，towards 也可用 to。

phrases.usage: 常搭 have/create a domino effect on sth。
phrases.example: The ruling had a domino effect on other firms. 该裁决对其他公司产生了连锁效应。

phrases.usage: make progress 的被动不定式形式，常与 there is still 连用。
phrases.example: There is still progress to be made on safety. 安全方面仍有待改进。

phrases.usage: attitude 可数，常用复数表泛指；后接 to/towards。
phrases.example: Attitudes towards remote work are shifting. 人们对远程办公的态度在变。

pitfalls: 第二个宾语从句保留 that：因为前面有 but，不保留会读成两个独立分句。
has witnessed 是现在完成时，不能改成一般过去时（since 标志）。
progress 不可数，不说 a progress / progresses。
analysis.paragraphRole: 借当事人之口做阶段性总结：制度层面已有连锁反应，观念层面仍待推进。

paragraphs.text: "I do think there's still some way to go...there's still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to essentially come right back to work, but I think the research is showing that's starting to change." He said equal parental leave is an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace. "The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking doesn't apply and hasn't applied for a long time."

sentences.text: "I do think there's still some way to go...there's still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to essentially come right back to work, but I think the research is showing that's starting to change."

analysis.senseInContext: 期待、期望（对新爸爸的隐性期待）
examples: Expectations for new fathers have barely changed. 对新爸爸的期待几乎没有改变。

confusables: expectancy（n. 期待，多用于 life expectancy）

analysis.translationLiteral: 「我确实认为还有一段路要走……对新爸爸来说，那种未明说的期待基本上还是会存在——即马上回去上班；但我认为研究显示这种情况正在开始改变。」
analysis.translationNatural: 「我确实觉得还有一段路要走……对新爸爸的那种『没说出口的期待』依然在——基本上就是赶紧回来上班；不过我觉得研究显示，这情况已经开始变了。」
analysis.structMarkup: "【I】 _do think_ ~{there's still some way to go}~... {there's still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to essentially come right back to work}, {but} 【I】 _think_ {the research is showing that's starting to change}."
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + 宾语从句 + 存在句并列 + but 转折主谓宾从句

components.part: there's still some way to go
there's still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to come right back to work
components.note: there is going to be 表将来存在

components.part: I think the research is showing that's starting to change

clauses: do think：助动词 do 表强调，口语常见（I do believe / I do agree）。
there's still some way to go：固定表达，意为「还有一段路要走」。
there's going to be ... expectation for sb to do sth：将来存在句 + 不定式作后置定语。
the research is showing (that) that's starting to change：两个 that，前者连词可省，后者是代词作主语。

phrases.meaning: 还有一段路要走、尚需努力
phrases.usage: 常用 there is still some way to go；也可说 a long way to go。
phrases.example: We still have some way to go on equality. 平等这件事我们还有很长的路要走。

phrases.meaning: 未明说的期待、潜规则式期待
phrases.usage: unstated 表「未言明的」；常用来指无形的社会压力。
phrases.example: There is an unstated expectation to work late. 存在一种不加班的隐性期待。

phrases.usage: right 在此是副词，表「立即、马上」。
phrases.example: She came right back to work after the weekend. 周末一过她马上回来上班。

pitfalls: I do think 的 do 是强调用法，不是「做」。
that's starting to change：that 是代词（指前述情况），不是连词。
sort of 是口语模糊语（「有点儿」），不表分类。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用受访者原话呈现「双重现实」——隐性期待未消，但趋势已变，为结论铺路。

sentences.text: He said equal parental leave is an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace.

analysis.senseInContext: 必不可少的、本质的（育儿假平等是必要一环）
examples: Sleep is essential for health. 睡眠对健康必不可少。

confusables: essential 后接 that 从句常用虚拟语气

analysis.senseInContext: 组成部分、要素（职场性别平等的必要一环）
examples: Feedback is a key component of learning. 反馈是学习的关键环节。

more.roots: com-（一起）+ ponere（放置）→ 放在一起的部分

analysis.translationLiteral: 他说，平等的育儿假是在职场创造性别平等的必要组成部分。
analysis.translationNatural: 他说，想在职场实现性别平等，男女一样的育儿假是必不可少的一环。
analysis.structMarkup: 【He】 _said_ ~{equal parental leave is an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + 宾语从句（从句为主系表）

components.part: an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace

clauses: an essential component to doing sth：to 是介词，后接动名词。
equal parental leave 作主语视为不可数概念，谓语用 is。
in the workplace 限定 gender equality 的范围。

phrases.meaning: 必要组成部分、不可或缺的一环
phrases.usage: 后接 of 或 to + 名词/动名词。
phrases.example: Trust is an essential component of teamwork. 信任是团队合作不可或缺的一环。

phrases.usage: 固定搭配；相关词 gender gap（性别差距）。
phrases.example: The firm publishes a gender equality report. 公司发布性别平等报告。

pitfalls: component to creating 中的 to 是介词，不能接动词原形。
essential 表「必不可少的」，比 important 语气强。
workplace 是一个词（工作场所），不写成 work place。
analysis.paragraphRole: 把前文的经验上升为原则性判断：育儿假平等是职场性别平等的前提。

sentences.text: "The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking doesn't apply and hasn't applied for a long time."

analysis.translationLiteral: 「女性留在家里、生孩子、做饭的旧标准不适用了，而且已经很久不适用了。」
analysis.translationNatural: 「『女的就该待在家里、生孩子、做饭』那套老规矩早就不成立了，而且已经很久不成立了。」
analysis.structMarkup: "【The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking】 _doesn't apply_ {and} _hasn't applied_ (for a long time)."
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓（两个并列谓语）+ 时间状语

components.part: The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking
components.note: of + 动名词复合结构作后置定语
一般现在时，表当前不成立
现在完成时，表持续状态

clauses: of women staying home, having babies and cooking：of + 动名词复合结构，women 是三个动名词的逻辑主语。
两个谓语时态不同：doesn't apply（现在不适用）+ hasn't applied（已经很久不适用），形成递进。
for a long time 与现在完成时搭配，不能用一般现在时。

phrases.usage: 此处 apply 不及物，表「适用」；表「申请」时用 apply for。

more.confusables: claim to do（声称）/ claim doing（不常用）

examples: They claim a strong desire for equality. 他们声称强烈渴望平等。

more.confusables: equality（平等）/ equity（公平）/ equation（方程）

vast.sense: 巨大的、广阔的；（the vast majority）绝大多数
examples: The vast majority of men said sharing care was a top reason. 绝大多数男性说分担照护是首要理由。

more.confusables: vast（巨大的）/ large（大的）/ huge（巨大的，口语）

examples: The majority of men admitted the female did most. 多数男性承认主要是女性在做。

more.confusables: majority（多数）/ most（大多数，更通用）/ minority（少数）

share.sense: 分享、分担（share sth with sb）；份额
examples: They want to share caregiving with their partner. 他们想与伴侣分担照护。

more.confusables: share（分享/分担）/ split（拆分）/ divide（划分）

caregiving.sense: 照护（对儿童、老人等的照料，不可数）
examples: They want to share caregiving with their partner. 他们想与伴侣分担照护。

more.confusables: caregiving（一个词）/ care giving（分写，较少见）

examples: Splitting tasks fairly matters. 公平分担任务很重要。

more.confusables: task（任务）/ work（工作）/ chore（家务杂事）

examples: Their experiences were considerably different. 他们的经历相当不同。

more.confusables: different from（英式常用）/ different than（美式口语）/ different to（英式口语）

examples: Both genders feared an impact on progress. 两性都担心影响发展。

more.confusables: genders（性别，复数）/ gender（单数）

examples: Companies need to give men paternity leave. 公司需要给男性陪产假。

more.confusables: give sb sth / give sth to sb（双宾语两种形式）/ give up（放弃）

care.sense: 照护、关心（不可数）；在乎（care about）、照顾（care for）
examples: Both genders should give the same amount of care. 两性应承担同等照护。

more.confusables: care about（在乎）/ care for（照顾/喜欢）/ take care of（照料）

reality.sense: 现实、实际情况（可数/不可数）
examples: In reality, the female did most of the care. 现实中主要是女性在做照护。

more.confusables: in reality（实际上）/ reality（现实）/ real（真实的）

female.sense: 女性的、雌性的 / 女性（可数）
examples: In reality the female actually did most of it. 现实主要还是女性在做。

more.confusables: female（女性，生物属性）/ woman（女人，社会属性）；反义 male

actually.sense: 实际上、事实上；居然（表出乎意料）
examples: In reality the female actually did most of it. 现实中主要还是女性在做。

more.confusables: actually（实际上）/ currently（目前）/ in fact（事实上）

examples: Only a tiny fraction of men did more childcare. 只有极小一部分男性承担更多育儿。

more.confusables: tiny（极小的）/ small（小的）/ little（少/小）

examples: Only 2% of men did more childcare—a tiny fraction. 只有 2% 的男性承担更多育儿。

more.confusables: fraction（部分/分数）/ fracture（断裂）/ faction（派系）

examples: Companies enhance women's advancement. 公司促进女性的职业发展。

more.confusables: women's（复数所有格，撇号在 s 后）/ woman's（单数所有格）

examples: Men and women's experiences differ. 男女的经历不同。

more.confusables: experiences（经历，可数）/ experience（经验，不可数）

following.sense: 接下来的；在……之后（介词）；跟随（分词）
examples: In the following two years he lost the title. 接下来两年他失去了冠军。

more.confusables: following（接下来的/在……之后）/ follow（跟随）

examples: Job satisfaction dropped for many women. 许多女性的工作满意度下降了。

more.confusables: job（职位，可数）/ work（工作，不可数）/ career（职业生涯）

examples: Job satisfaction fell for many women. 许多女性的工作满意度下降。

more.confusables: satisfaction（满意）/ satisfactory（令人满意的）/ satisfied（感到满意的）

increased.sense: increase 的过去式/过去分词（增加）；增加的
examples: 14% said job satisfaction increased. 14% 说工作满意度上升了。

more.confusables: increased（增加的，作定语）/ increasing（不断增加的）

examples: Job satisfaction went down for 32% of women. 32% 的女性工作满意度下降。

more.confusables: went（go 的过去式）/ gone（过去分词）

examples: Meanwhile, more women reported an increase in responsibilities. 同时，更多女性报告责任增加。

more.confusables: meanwhile（同时，连接副词）/ while（当……时/然而）

increase.sense: 增加（动词读 /ɪnˈkriːs/）；增加（名词读 /ˈɪnkriːs/）
examples: More women reported an increase in responsibilities. 更多女性报告责任增加。

more.confusables: increase（动词）/ increase in（名词 + 介词）

examples: More women reported an increase in responsibilities. 更多女性报告职责增加。

more.confusables: responsibility（责任）/ responsible（负责的）/ response（回应）

used.sense: use 的过去式/过去分词；（be used to）习惯于；（used to）过去常常
examples: They used flexible work arrangements. 他们使用了弹性工作安排。

more.confusables: used to do（过去常常）/ be used to doing（习惯于）/ be used to do（被用来做）

becoming.sense: become 的现在分词（变得、成为）；合适的（形容词）
examples: After becoming a parent, they used flexible work. 成为父母后，他们使用弹性工作。

more.confusables: becoming（现在分词/合适的）/ become（变成）

parent.sense: 父亲或母亲（可数）；母公司（作定语）
examples: They used flexible arrangements after becoming a parent. 他们成为父母后使用弹性安排。

more.confusables: parent（父母任一方）/ parents（父母双方）

examples: Men reported similar levels of enjoyment. 男性报告的享受程度相近。

more.confusables: similar to（与……相似）/ the same as（与……相同）

sense.sense: 感觉、意识（a sense of）；意义；感官 / 感觉到
examples: Work gave them a sense of achievement. 工作给他们成就感。

more.confusables: make sense（讲得通）/ a sense of（……感）/ sense（感官）

examples: It is key to model good behavior. 以身作则很关键。

more.confusables: key to（……的关键，to 为介词）/ key（钥匙）

examples: On the subject of career advancement, 59% worried. 谈到职业晋升，59% 表示担忧。

more.confusables: advancement（晋升/发展）/ advance（前进/提前）/ advanced（高级的）

progress.sense: 进步、进展（不可数）/ 前进、进展
examples: There is still progress to be made. 仍有进展要做。

more.confusables: progress（不可数，不说 a progress）/ progress 作动词读 /prəˈɡres/

examples: Leave could have a long-term impact. 休假可能有长期影响。

more.confusables: long-term（形容词/副词，带连字符）/ in the long term（短语，长期）

examples: The online world offers remarkable opportunities. 网络世界提供难得机会。

more.confusables: opportunity（良机，正面）/ chance（机会/可能性，中性）

promotion.sense: 晋升（不可数/可数）；促销、推广
examples: Women believed their chances of promotion were lower. 女性认为自己的晋升机会更低。

more.confusables: promotion（晋升/推广）/ promote（提升/推广）/ promotional（促销的）

chances.sense: 机会、可能性（chance 的复数）
examples: Data increases the chances of success. 数据能提高成功的机会。

more.confusables: chance（机会）/ opportunity（良机，偏正面）/ by chance（偶然）

lower.sense: 降低（动词）；更低的（low 的比较级）
examples: Social life can lower stress levels. 社交生活能降低压力水平。

more.confusables: lower（降低/更低）/ low（低的）/ lose（失去）

despite.sense: 尽管、虽然（后接名词或动名词，不接从句）
examples: Despite progress, women still struggle. 尽管有进步，女性仍在艰难争取。

more.confusables: despite + 名词（不是从句）/ although + 从句

struggle.sense: 挣扎、努力（struggle to do / struggle with）；斗争
examples: They struggle with new communication skills. 他们在新沟通技能上挣扎。

more.confusables: struggle to do（努力做，含困难）/ try to do（尝试）/ struggle with（应对困难）

power.sense: 力量、权力（不可数）；动力 / 驱动
examples: Women struggle to reach positions of power. 女性难以进入权力高位。

more.confusables: power（权力/力量）/ strength（体力）

mean.sense: 意味着、意思是；打算 / 吝啬的、刻薄的
examples: This would mean the end of a career. 这就意味着职业生涯的终结。

more.confusables: mean to do（打算做）/ mean doing（意味着）

need.sense: 需要（情态/实义动词）；需要、需求（名词）
examples: Parents need to set boundaries. 家长需要划定界限。

more.confusables: need to do（实义动词）/ need do（情态动词，多用于否定疑问）

encourage.sense: 鼓励、促进（encourage sb to do）；助长
examples: Social life encourages positive health behaviours. 社交生活促进积极健康行为。

more.confusables: encourage sb to do（不是 doing）/ discourage（反义）

examples: Kids adapt quickly to new tools. 孩子对新工具适应很快。

more.confusables: kid（口语：孩子）/ child（正式：孩子）

examples: Companies must support men early on. 公司必须在早期就支持男性。

more.confusables: early（早）/ soon（不久）/ earlier（更早）

examples: A rich social life improves health. 丰富的社交生活能改善健康。

more.confusables: life（单数）/ lives（复数，注意拼写）

significant.sense: 显著的、重要的；统计上显著的
examples: Loneliness is a significant problem. 孤独是个重要问题。

more.confusables: significant（显著的）/ significance（意义）

cannot.sense: 不能（can 的否定形式，写成一个词）
examples: Companies cannot do all these things and then turn around. 公司不能做了这些又反过来改口。

more.confusables: cannot（一个词，正式）/ can not（分写，多用于强调 not）/ can't（口语缩写）

examples: They have to do all these things first. 他们必须先做所有这些事。

more.confusables: things（事情/东西）/ stuff（东西，不可数，口语）

enhance.sense: 提升、增强（质量、能力）；促进
examples: Companies enhance women's advancement. 公司促进女性的职业发展。

more.confusables: enhance（提升质量/价值）/ increase（增加数量）/ improve（改善）

examples: Kids don't lack patience. 孩子并不缺耐心。

more.confusables: don't（do not）/ doesn't（does not）/ didn't（did not）

examples: They announced a $5m settlement. 他们宣布了 500 万美元和解。

more.confusables: settlement（和解/定居点）/ settle（解决/定居）

male.sense: 男性的、雄性的 / 男性
examples: Male employees claimed they were denied leave. 男员工称他们被拒绝休假。

more.confusables: male（男性）/ man（男人）；反义 female

access.sense: 接触机会、使用权（不可数）/ 访问、获取
examples: They were denied access to paid leave. 他们被拒绝享有带薪假。

more.confusables: access（接触/访问）/ excess（过度）

examples: The company changed its leave policy. 该公司修改了休假政策。

more.confusables: company（公司/陪伴）/ companion（同伴）

examples: His HR department told him mothers came first. 他的人事部门告诉他母亲优先。

more.confusables: department（部门）/ division（分部）/ section（科/部分）

considered.sense: consider 的过去式/过去分词（认为、考虑）
examples: Mothers were considered primary caregivers. 母亲被视为主要照护者。

more.confusables: consider doing（考虑做）/ consider sb to be（认为某人是）

primary.sense: 主要的；初级的；初等教育的
examples: Mothers were considered primary caregivers. 母亲被视为主要照护者。

more.confusables: primary（首要的/初级的）/ prime（首要的/全盛期）/ secondary（次要的）

allowed.sense: allow 的过去式/过去分词（允许）
examples: Mothers were allowed 16 weeks of leave. 母亲被允许休 16 周假。

more.confusables: be allowed to do（被允许）/ be allowed doing（错误）/ allow for（考虑到）

associate.sense: 同事、副职（名词）；联系（动词，be associated with）
examples: He works as an associate and investigator. 他担任副理兼调查员。

more.confusables: associate（同事/联系）/ association（协会/关联）

examples: The settlement had a domino effect. 和解产生了连锁效应。

more.confusables: effect（名词）/ affect（动词）/ take effect（生效）

changing.sense: change 的现在分词；不断变化的
examples: They spend hours changing Facebook settings. 他们花数小时修改 Facebook 设置。

more.confusables: changing（正在变的）/ changed（已变的）

examples: Many think the risk is small. 很多人认为风险很小。

more.confusables: think about（考虑）/ think of（想起）/ think over（仔细考虑）

there's.sense: there is 或 there has 的缩写
examples: There's still some way to go. 还有一段路要走。

more.confusables: there's（there is）/ theirs（他们的）

way.sense: 方法、方式；路；程度（in a way）
collocations: the best way to do sth
examples: There is no simple way to fix it. 没有简单的办法解决它。

more.confusables: way（方法）/ road（道路）/ method（方法，正式）

go.sense: 去、走；（go up/down）上升/下降；进行
collocations: there is still some way to go
examples: Satisfaction went down for many women. 许多女性满意度下降。

more.confusables: go up/down（上升/下降，口语）/ increase/decrease（正式）

going.sense: go 的现在分词；（be going to）将要
examples: Attitudes are going to change. 态度将会改变。

more.confusables: be going to（计划/预测）/ will（临时决定或预测）

examples: Fewer readers come from that background. 来自那种背景的读者更少。

more.confusables: come（来）/ go（去）

right.sense: 正确的；右边的；恰恰（副词）/ 权利
examples: They come right back to work. 他们马上回去上班。

more.confusables: right（正确/右/权利）/ write（写）/ rite（仪式）

back.sense: 回、向后（副词）；背部；后面的 / 支持（动词）
examples: Fewer kids come right back to reading. 更少孩子会马上回到阅读。

more.confusables: back（回/背部）/ backward（向后的）

examples: That's what I think I'm supposed to say. 我以为自己「应该」这么说。

more.confusables: that's why（所以）/ that's because（那是因为）

essential.sense: 必不可少的、本质的；要素（复数）
examples: Equal leave is an essential component. 平等休假是不可或缺的一环。

more.confusables: essential to（对……必不可少）/ essential（本质的）/ necessary（必要的）

examples: The old standard no longer applies. 旧标准不再适用。

more.confusables: old（老/旧）/ older（更老）/ elder（年长的，仅指人）

doesn't.sense: does not 的缩写（第三人称单数否定）
examples: That doesn't mean it's all good news. 这并不意味着全是好消息。

more.confusables: doesn't（does not）/ don't（do not，复数或第一二人称）

applied.sense: apply 的过去式/过去分词（应用、申请）；应用的
examples: The method can be applied to teaching. 这个方法可应用于教学。

more.confusables: apply to（适用于）/ apply for（申请）/ applied（应用的）

long.sense: 长的、长期的 / 长久地
examples: The impact is long-term. 影响是长期的。

more.confusables: long（长）/ lengthy（冗长的）/ as long as（只要）
